● Review target: hermit feat/pressure-test-resume-20261028, 4c98a7a0..5f28407ff0ed2ad410c03f9279baeb466c783dc8. Below, P is
  ci/compat-envelope/pressure-test.rs and R is ci/manifest-plan/src/runner.rs.

  Verdict on H3: changes requested, narrowly. run --resume now meets the original requirement: it never combines observations from a different binary or
  test inside the run. One gap remains, in standalone summarize. Separately, batch runs check the wrong checkout before running, which causes false
  refusals and wasted runs but never accepts mixed rows.

  Findings

  1. Medium (the remaining requirement gap): standalone summarize builds verdicts from mixed-identity rows.
     - After the post-run check at P:4433 refuses, the results directory still holds everything: old rows, new rows, the merged runner-outcomes.json
       (written at P:4409, before the check) and the filtered dag.json.
     - summarize --results DIR (P:4487, then summarize at P:11749) recognises the resumed shape through standalone_resume_completed (P:11773). It then
       judges the rows through summarize_with_resume_durable (P:11810).
     - The summary path never checks binary or test identity. binary_sha256 only appears in P:2519–2717 and in merge at P:3076–3099.
     - So rows from two different binaries can still become cell verdicts. The H2 fix added this path.
     - Required change: when summarize sees the resumed shape, run verify_resume_identities, or at least require one binary and one test digest per
       test. Alternatively, leave a marker after a refused resume that summarize refuses.
     - This is a static trace; I did not run it.
  2. Medium: batch runs check the wrong checkout. This wastes runs and refuses wrongly; it does not accept mixed rows.
     - For a batch run, prepare_resume(&root) runs at P:4245, before enter_fresh_checkout at P:4284.
     - The pre-run check therefore hashes root/target/ci/hermit. If that file is missing, it runs cargo build in the root checkout (P:2577–2611).
     - But the durable rows recorded the previous fresh checkout's binary. The cells will run a new fresh checkout's binary: a new mktemp directory
       every run (P:1715), unless --reuse-fresh-checkout reuses pressure-fresh-<sha> (P:1758).
     - Outcome: almost always a false refusal, because Hermit builds are not bit-reproducible. That includes the --reuse-fresh-checkout case, where the
       binary that actually runs might match the rows.
     - If the root binary happens to match, the missing repetitions run on a rebuilt binary and P:4433 refuses only after the whole campaign has run.
     - plan --resume (P:4163), which is meant to be inspection-only, can also start a cargo build in the root checkout.
     - Fix: run the identity check against the fresh checkout after its build step and before the cell steps.
  3. Low: rows with no binary hash refuse the whole resume, with a misleading message.
     - The harness writes binary_sha256 = None by design for host-inapplicable rows (R:9318), and binary_digest can also return None at R:9239.
     - P:2519–2531 refuses any such row and says to "restore rows written by the current harness", but the current harness wrote it. It fails closed,
       but it blocks legitimate campaigns.

  Evidence that the core requirement is met

  - What the producer records: R:9105–9106 and R:9152–9153 write binary_sha256 = binary_digest(context.hermit_bin) and test_sha256 = test_digest(...).
  - The binary that runs is the one that is hashed: cells run HERMIT_BIN="$PWD/target/ci/hermit" (P:151, P:8257), with the working directory set to the
    execution root (P:4087–4094, P:4344).
  - Post-run check: P:4432–4433 runs verify_resume_identities(execution_root, …) over every durable row, old and new, before summarize at P:4435.
    P:2669–2693 refuses any binary-hash or test-digest mismatch. So within run, a changed binary or test at the same HEAD and path is refused.
  - Exact-cell build order is coherent:
    - allows_dirty_source (P:1133) means no fresh checkout (P:4276–4283), so the root and the execution root are the same.
    - The pre-run check (P:4566–4567) rebuilds a missing target/ci/hermit (P:2568–2621).
    - The build.e2e_artifact step then skips because the marker exists and target/ci/hermit is executable (P:7436–7449, P:8034–8038). The hashed binary
      is therefore the one that runs.
    - If the marker is missing, the step rebuilds after the check, and P:4433 catches the difference.
    - One caveat: the error text tells the user to rebuild and rerun, which will keep refusing while builds are not bit-reproducible.
  - Merge: P:3076–3099 requires one binary hash and one test digest per test across all attempt directories. That is correct, though it always refuses
    separately built w1/w2 campaigns.
  - Was HEAD + tree + existence enough? No, and it is no longer the rule. Comparing digests against the durable rows is the right standard, and equality
    is the right comparison. No bar was lowered.
  - What test_sha256 means (R:10261): the SHA-256 of the test.program source bytes, or else the JSON encoding of the direct command
    (Option<Vec<String>>; null when the test has neither). It does not cover the compiled guest, the toolchain, host executables found through PATH, or
    manifest fields such as mode, environment, timeouts and expected exit status.
  - Not recorded in rows at all: test-harness and DBT/LiteInst runtime digests, so resume cannot check those.

  Goalpost-moving assessment
  - Assertions weakened: no.
  - Tolerance widened, exemption added, case skipped or comparator relaxed: no. The digest comparison is stricter than round 2.
  - Failure relabelled as a pass: only through the summarize path in finding 1.
  - Check deleted instead of satisfied: no.
  - Test coverage: the self-tests (P:17948–18100) cover the merge refusals, the rebuild, and binary and test mismatches at the unit level. Nothing
    exercises prepare_resume end to end, the batch fresh-checkout path, or summarize after a refused resume.
